deep.reconstruction:
This page sets up the bookkeeping for classifying arrangements of pseudolines ('systèmes de pseudo-droites') in the real projective plane X ≅ P²(ℝ), with Σ the set of pseudolines.

Setup:
- I is an index set with card I = n+1. A point i0 ∈ I is chosen, and I0 = I∖{i0}.
- C(I) is the set of isomorphism classes of I-labelled ('I-épinglés') arrangements (X, Σ = (Δ_i)_{i∈I}).
- Taking Δ_{i0} as the line at infinity identifies C(I) with C_aff(I0), the I0-labelled affine arrangements of n pseudolines. The complement of a pseudoline in P² is an open disc.
- The symmetric groups 𝔖_I ⊃ 𝔖_{I0} act by relabelling.

The diagram (the first version is struck out and redrawn):
- α: C(I) → C_aff(n) ≅ C_aff(I0)/𝔖_{I0} ≅ C(I)/𝔖_{I0}. It forgets the labelling except for the distinguished line Δ = Δ_{i0}. So C_aff(n) = iso classes of triples (X, Σ, Δ), with (X, Σ) an arrangement of n+1 pseudolines and Δ ∈ Σ marked.
- β: C_aff(n) → C(n+1) ≅ C(I)/𝔖_I forgets which line is marked.
- β': C_aff(n) → C(n) erases Δ ('gommage de Δ'), leaving an arrangement Σ* = Σ∖{Δ} of n pseudolines.

Fibres:
- β is surjective. Its fibre over cl(X, Σ) is the set of types of elements of Σ, i.e. the orbit set Σ/G_{X,Σ} under the automorphism group of the arrangement.
- β' is noted 'surjective (?)'. Its fibre over cl(X, Σ*) is the set of types of relative position of an added pseudoline with respect to (X, Σ*), i.e. one-element extensions modulo automorphisms.

Numerical checks (simple arrangements):
- n+1 = 6: C(6) has 4 elements, with fibres of β of sizes 1, 1, 2, 2.
- n = 5: C(5) has one element, and the fibre of β' is said to have card 5.

NB: the 'stable' arrangements C_st(I) = C_aff st(I0) ⊂ C_aff(I0) are presumably the simple ones (no three lines concurrent; stable under perturbation). This subset is 𝔖_I-stable, so the same diagram descends to C_st(I), C_aff st(n), C_st(n), C_st(n+1).

Purpose: a recursive or double-counting scheme to enumerate projective pseudoline arrangements, using marked-line affine arrangements as intermediaries. The next page encodes such an arrangement as a stable system of chords in a disc D = Déc(X, Δ), whose boundary is the double cover of Δ. This is essentially the wiring-diagram / allowable-sequence encoding.
errors: β' surjectivity, marked '(?)', is actually true: it is Levi's enlargement lemma (1926), which lets a pseudoline be added through any two points, hence extending any arrangement.

Possible numerical inconsistency. The β-fibres for n+1 = 6 sum to 1+1+2+2 = 6, so C_aff st(5) has 6 elements. This agrees with the known count of 6 simple Euclidean arrangements of 5 pseudolines. Since C_st(5) has a single element, the β'-fibre must then be the whole domain, of card 6, not 5 as written. Either one of the counts is a slip, or a different equivalence (e.g. mirror images) is being used in one of them. I am working from memory and have not verified this independently.

ideas.what: Projective arrangements with a marked line ↔ affine (disc) arrangements; labelled and unlabelled classification spaces related by symmetric-group quotients
ideas.modern_name: Euclidean vs projective pseudoline arrangements; marked arrangements

ideas.what: Fibre of forgetting the marked line is the set of automorphism orbits of lines
ideas.modern_name: orbit–stabilizer / double counting of marked arrangements

ideas.what: Fibre of deleting a line is the set of relative-position types of a new pseudoline (extensions)
ideas.modern_name: single-element extensions of rank-3 oriented matroids; Levi enlargement lemma
ideas.usually_credited_to: Levi; Las Vergnas; Bokowski–Sturmfels and others for enumeration

ideas.what: Restriction to 'stable' (simple) arrangements, compatible with all the quotient maps

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine setup for the enumeration of pseudoline arrangements, all standard in the Goodman–Pollack/Grünbaum literature. The only notable item is a small internal counting inconsistency (5 vs 6).
